correctness.rationale: PASS: Checked the operator acts on monomial z^beta w^b as rho^b (N+b)/(N+b+k) z^beta w^(b+k), with N=|beta|; normalized target monomials are distinct, so the singular values are exactly their weight ratios (rather than merely comparable). Reconstructed the Fubini/Beta monomial squared norm pi^n beta!/(b+1) Gamma(1+(b+1)/m)/Gamma(N+n+(b+1)/m). Fixed-b gamma quotient yields sigma_{N,b}~rho^b A_b N^{-k/(2m)} and multiplicity binom(N+n-2,n-2), giving p*=2m(n-1)/k and coefficient (n-1)!^{-1}sum_b rho^{b p*}A_b^{p*}. The uniform gamma ratio bound C rho^b(1+b)^a(1+N)^(-a) ensures a summable degree-by-degree counting envelope for every fixed rho<1; rho=0 leaves b=0 only. A_b^{p*}~m^{-(n-1)}b^{n-1}, and standard Abelian series asymptotics give (1-rho)^n L ->m^{-(n-1)}p*^{-n}; this order of limits is essential. At rho=1, fixed N and b->infty makes singular weight tend to 1 on orthogonal columns, giving essential norm=norm=1; rho<1 compact, converges strongly but distance always 1. Independent numerical checks recomputed 16 exact gamma/singular-value specializations (n=m=k=2, b=0,1,3,9 and N=1,5,30,100), and the closed constant L=1/[2(1-rho²)^2] at rho=0,.2,.5,.8; all agree to floating precision. These finite numerical checks corroborate but do not prove the Weyl law.
